AGENDA
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  AUGUST 05, 2019
  4:00 PM

  1. ROLL CALL

  2. CONSENT ITEMS
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by
  making such request before motion is proposed.

  a. Approval of the minutes for the July 01, 2019 Meeting

  3. GWP COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS

  4. REPORTS - INFORMATION
  a.  Public Health Goal – 2019 Report
  b.  Water Division Consumer Confidence Report
  c.  Legislative Update
  d.  Customer Service Update
  e.  Water Resource Update

  5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS (5) Minutes
  Discussion is limited to items NOT part of this agenda. Each speaker is allowed five (5) minutes – Commission may question or respond to the speaker, but there
  will be no debate or decision. The General Manager may refer the matter to appropriate staff for investigation and report.

  6. AGENDA FORECAST

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  SPECIAL MEETING: Next Meeting is scheduled for September 5, 2019

Welcome to the meeting of the Glendale Water & Power Commission. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office by calling (818) 548-2090. Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
www.ci.glendale.ca.us/video_archives.asp. PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES AND PAGERS WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the GWP Administration Office 141 N.
Glendale Avenue 4th Floor, Glendale, CA 91206. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact Catalina Lee (818) 548-2107 during regular
business hours.
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  COUNCIL CHAMBER, City Hall – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206

  August 5, 2019
  4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  Present: President Avanessian, Commissioners Carrasco, Kedikian, Lall and Watson

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the July 1, 2019 Meeting Minutes
  Motion to Approve as Amended (with corrected spelling of Commissioner Carrasco’s last name
  under “Roll Call”):
  Moved by: Commissioner Watson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Commissioner Lall applauded the GWP Commission, staff, City Council, and especially the
  members of the public for a successful outcome in the approval of the Integrated Resource Plan,
  the Clean Energy RFP and the discussions regarding the future of the Grayson Power Plant. She
  noted that the result was a collaborative effort with input from the public which will lead to a cleaner
  environment for Glendale and the surrounding community. President Avanessian thanked GWP
  crews for their work during the hot weather, and noted that outages have been really limited.
  Commissioner Carrasco thanked the Commission and staff for their work on the IRP and Grayson
  discussion. He complimented GWP on providing updates and keeping the public informed during
  the recent power outage.

4. REPORTS – INFORMATION
  a. Public Health Goal – 2019 Report. Mr. James Saenz, GWP Water Quality Manager, reported
  on GWP’s compliance with public health goals (PHGs) for the 2016-2018 periods, per California
  Health and Safety Code Section 116470(b). Mr. Saenz noted that PHGs are health based goals but
  are not enforceable, while Maximum Contaminant Levels (MCLs) are legally enforceable
  requirements. Mr. Saenz reported on three contaminants that have been detected above the PHG
  level in select samples during the 2016-2018 periods: total coliform, nitrate, and
  tetrachloroethylene. Mr. Saenz described how each of these constituents are managed to ensure
  healthy and safe drinking water for the public. In response to Commissioners’ questions, Mr. Saenz
  stated that GWP publishes an annual water quality report as required by law, and produces a PHG
  report every three years. Nitrates mainly come from historical use of fertilizers in the foothill area.
  The Foothill well is a small well on Foothill and it is blended with water from a large reservoir before
  being served to customers.
 b. Water Division Consumer Confidence Report. Mr. Martin Manucharyan, GWP Water Quality
Supervisor, presented GWP’s annual water quality report. He described the history of water quality
management and described key regulations, including the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, the
Clean Water Act, and the Safe Drinking Water Act. Mr. Manucharyan explained that the Consumer
Confident Report provides last year’s water quality sampling results, and the report is available by
July 1 of each year at www.glendalewaterandpower.com, as well as in hard copy form upon request
to GWP.

In response to Commissioners’ questions, Mr. Manucharyan stated that customers with questions
about their water quality could reach him at (818) 548-2011. He explained that customers may on
occasion have a chorine smell or taste to their water because chlorine is used in water treatment;
when this occurs, the water can be flushed by running the tap for a little while. In response
Commissioner Carrasco’s question about automation of disinfection systems, Mr. De Ghetto
reported that disinfection systems for wells operate in conjunction with the wells and during an
electrical power outage, the wells do not pump water to the reservoirs. The reservoirs continue to
serve water to the customers via gravity. The Glendale Operable Unit water treatment system stops
during an outage, and goes into a startup sequence when the power goes back online. Metropolitan
Water District water is delivered by gravity, including during an outage, and is enters the Glendale
system already with the proper disinfection levels added.

c. Legislative Update. Leo Zalyan, GWP Administrative Analyst, stated the legislature will
reconvene from summer recess on August 12, 2019, and September 13, 2019 will be the end of the
legislative session. Mr. Zalyan covered key electric and water bills. On the electric side, Mr. Zalyan
covered AB 1054 (a chaptered bill establishing a Wildfire Safety Advisory Board and annual
updates to Wildfire Management Plans); AB 1208 (Utility User’s Tax exemption for residential solar
production); AB 1799 (natural gas volatility study); AB 1424 (electrical vehicle station payment
options); SB 457 (in-state biomethane); SB 560 (wildfire management); SB 676 (electrical vehicle
integration study); and SB 772 (pumped storage). On the water side, Mr. Zalyan covered AB 1180
(backflow prevention); AB 60 (water meter accuracy); AB 1414 (streamlining water reporting); AB
134 (water loss performance standards); SB 200 (a chaptered bill assisting water systems to
provide safe drinking water); SB 203 (State Water Project noticing); and SB 313 (Small Water
System Authority Act of 2019). Commissioner Watson suggested that GWP present GWP’s position
on the bills in a future update, and Commissioner Carrasco suggested that it would be good to
know how bills that are passed affect GWP. Mr. Zalyan concurred. In response to a question from
Commissioner Kedikian, Mr. Zalyan stated that GWP would not receive funds under SB 200, as that
is for water systems that are failing.

d. Customer Service Update. Ms. Tami Vallier, Customer Services Administrator, presented
customer service highlights comparing the years 2017-19 and 2018-19 with regard to key metrics in
target areas, including customer service, billing and account maintenance, and field operations.
President Avanessian asked if the percentage increases and decrease from year to year take into
account changes in population. Ms. Vallier responded that the results are not presented in that way
currently, but it is something that could be analyzed in the future. Mr. De Ghetto added that number
of accounts would be a more appropriate metric than population changes. Ms. Vallier described the
effect of the July 24, 2019 power outage on call volume. Call volume spiked during the outage, but
through a team effort, GWP was able to handle most of the calls. Commissioner Watson
complimented GWP on the handling of calls during the outage and its impressive performance.
Commissioner Carrasco inquired whether GWP conducts a customer satisfaction survey, and Ms.
Vallier affirmed that GWP conducts surveys of commercial and residential customers in alternating
years (one each year). GWP will be implementing a new phone system which will allow for follow up
surveys. GWP is also looking to get field follow up surveys underway, as well as web request follow
up via email.
   e. Water Resource Update. Chief Assistant General Manager Michael DeGhetto described
  GWP’s water sources and quantities. Mr. De Ghetto stated that local sources are the San Fernando
  and Verdugo Basins and the Los Angeles-Glendale Water Reclamation Plant, and imported
  sources from the Metropolitan Water District including water from the Colorado River Aqueduct and
  State Water Project. Mr. De Ghetto provided metrics on conservation and current water usage
  numbers for GWP customers, including annual trends, use by customer type, and the effect of
  temperature and precipitation. The numbers show that GWP customers continue to conserve since
  the City’s drought restrictions have been lifted. Mr. DeGhetto noted that GWP’s water system has
  the highest (Grade 5) complexity rating for distribution and treatment and Mr. DeGhetto highlighted
  the qualifications of GWP water staff. Commissioner Lall asked if the drought is over and Mr.
  DeGhetto responded that as a water manager, he does not think in terms of drought, but rather on
  the long term management of the water supply. Mr. De Ghetto outlined GWP’s efforts to continue to
  manage the water supply, including having 4 distinct sources of water and continued conservation.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  There were no changes made to the proposed Agenda Forecast for future meetings. Ms. Catalina Lee,
  GWP Office Services Supervisor, confirmed that the September 2019 meeting will be a special meeting
  on September 5, 2019 due to the Labor Day holiday.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Watson
  Seconded by: Commissioner Kedikian
  Motion Passed.
  The meeting was adjourned at 5:30 pm.
